```{r setup, include=FALSE}
SEED <- 1
DATA_PATH <- "../data/raw/heart_failure_clinical_records_dataset.csv"
FIGURE_PATH <- "../figures"

knitr::opts_chunk$set(
  echo = TRUE,
  warning = FALSE,
  message = FALSE,
  fig.align = "center",
  fig.width = 8,
  fig.height = 5,
  dpi = 160
)

library(dplyr)
library(tidyr)
library(ggplot2)
library(caret)
library(MASS)
library(pROC)
library(kernlab)
library(nnet)
library(MVN)
library(biotools)

dir.create(FIGURE_PATH, recursive = TRUE, showWarnings = FALSE)
set.seed(SEED)
```

# 1. Purpose

This project began as multivariate statistics coursework comparing LDA, QDA,
linear and RBF SVM, and an artificial neural network (ANN) for classifying
DEATH_EVENT. A portfolio review later found that the reported performances were
not directly comparable. LDA and QDA used cross-validation, SVM performance was
calculated by predicting the training data, and ANN performance came from one
hold-out split.

The updated question is:

> When LDA, QDA, SVM, and ANN models are evaluated under the same resampling
> design, how do their discrimination performance and error profiles differ?

The goal is to improve validation design and compare error trade-offs. The

# 2. Data and outcome

```{r load-data}
raw_data <- read.csv(DATA_PATH)

clinical_variables <- c(
  "age",
  "creatinine_phosphokinase",
  "ejection_fraction",
  "platelets",
  "serum_creatinine",
  "serum_sodium"
)

model_data <- raw_data |>
  dplyr::select(DEATH_EVENT, dplyr::all_of(clinical_variables)) |>
  mutate(
    # caret::twoClassSummary treats the first factor level as the event.
    DEATH_EVENT = factor(
      DEATH_EVENT,
      levels = c(1, 0),
      labels = c("Died", "Survived")
    )
  )

data_summary <- tibble(
  Patients = nrow(model_data),
  Deaths = sum(model_data$DEATH_EVENT == "Died"),
  Survivors = sum(model_data$DEATH_EVENT == "Survived"),
  Missing_values = sum(is.na(model_data))
)

knitr::kable(data_summary)
```

The dataset contains 299 patients, including 96 deaths and 203 survivors. No
missing values were found in the analysis variables.

The original dataset includes time, which records follow-up duration. It is not
used as an ordinary predictor because doing so would mix post-baseline follow-up
information with the classification target and could introduce target-related
leakage. This project is neither survival analysis nor prediction of mortality
at a fixed time horizon. No Cox model or Kaplan-Meier analysis is added.

# 3. Focused exploratory analysis

## 3.1 Observed group differences

```{r group-summary}
group_summary <- model_data |>
  group_by(DEATH_EVENT) |>
  summarise(
    across(
      all_of(clinical_variables),
      list(mean = mean, median = median),
      .names = "{.col}_{.fn}"
    ),
    .groups = "drop"
  )

knitr::kable(group_summary, digits = 2)
```

```{r group-boxplots, fig.cap="Observed distributions of six clinical variables by outcome group."}
boxplot_data <- model_data |>
  pivot_longer(
    cols = all_of(clinical_variables),
    names_to = "Variable",
    values_to = "Value"
  )

group_boxplot <- ggplot(
  boxplot_data,
  aes(x = DEATH_EVENT, y = Value, fill = DEATH_EVENT)
) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.65, outlier.alpha = 0.35) +
  facet_wrap(~ Variable, scales = "free_y", ncol = 3) +
  scale_fill_manual(values = c(Died = "#C44E52", Survived = "#4C72B0")) +
  labs(x = NULL, y = NULL, fill = "Outcome") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(
  file.path(FIGURE_PATH, "group_boxplots.png"),
  group_boxplot,
  width = 10,
  height = 6.5,
  dpi = 180
)

group_boxplot
```

The death group was older on average, had lower ejection fraction, higher serum
creatinine, and lower serum sodium. These are observed group differences only.
This analysis does not estimate adjusted effects, odds ratios, or causal risk
factors.

## 3.2 Correlation and discriminant-analysis assumptions

```{r correlation}
correlation_matrix <- model_data |>
  dplyr::select(all_of(clinical_variables)) |>
  cor()

knitr::kable(correlation_matrix, digits = 2)
```

```{r assumption-checks}
hz_died <- MVN::mvn(
  data = model_data |>
    filter(DEATH_EVENT == "Died") |>
    dplyr::select(all_of(clinical_variables)),
  mvn_test = "hz"
)

hz_survived <- MVN::mvn(
  data = model_data |>
    filter(DEATH_EVENT == "Survived") |>
    dplyr::select(all_of(clinical_variables)),
  mvn_test = "hz"
)

box_m <- biotools::boxM(
  model_data |> dplyr::select(all_of(clinical_variables)),
  grouping = model_data$DEATH_EVENT
)

assumption_results <- tibble(
  Test = c("Henze-Zirkler: Died", "Henze-Zirkler: Survived", "Box's M"),
  P_value = c(
    hz_died$multivariate_normality$p.value,
    hz_survived$multivariate_normality$p.value,
    box_m$p.value
  )
)

knitr::kable(assumption_results, digits = 5)
```

Multivariate normality was not supported in either group, and covariance
homogeneity was also rejected. LDA and QDA are retained as educational
comparators, but their results should be interpreted cautiously.

# 4. Original validation issues

| Model | Original evaluation | Main issue |
|---|---|---|
| LDA | Leave-one-out cross-validation | Different evaluation scheme |
| QDA | Leave-one-out cross-validation | Different scheme and priors reversed relative to factor levels |
| Linear SVM | Prediction on training data | Optimistic estimate |
| RBF SVM | Prediction on training data | Reported 2.68% error was training error |
| ANN | One 60:40 hold-out split | Split-dependent estimate; scaling preceded splitting |

The original coursework is preserved rather than silently corrected. Details are
recorded in docs/validation_changes.md.

# 5. Common validation design

The comparison uses stratified 5-fold cross-validation repeated 5 times, the
same training folds for every model, fold-internal centering and scaling, and
Died as the positive class. ROC-AUC is the tuning metric. Sensitivity,
specificity, balanced accuracy, and accuracy are reported alongside it. The seed
is fixed at 1 before fold creation and every model fit.

```{r create-folds}
set.seed(SEED)

cv_index <- createMultiFolds(
  y = model_data$DEATH_EVENT,
  k = 5,
  times = 5
)

length(cv_index)
```

```{r summary-and-control}
clinical_summary <- function(data, lev = NULL, model = NULL) {
  two_class <- caret::twoClassSummary(data = data, lev = lev, model = model)
  default <- caret::defaultSummary(data = data, lev = lev, model = model)

  c(
    ROC = unname(two_class["ROC"]),
    Sensitivity = unname(two_class["Sens"]),
    Specificity = unname(two_class["Spec"]),
    Balanced_Accuracy = unname(
      (two_class["Sens"] + two_class["Spec"]) / 2
    ),
    Accuracy = unname(default["Accuracy"])
  )
}

ctrl <- trainControl(
  method = "repeatedcv",
  number = 5,
  repeats = 5,
  index = cv_index,
  classProbs = TRUE,
  summaryFunction = clinical_summary,
  savePredictions = "final",
  allowParallel = FALSE
)
```

# 6. Model fitting

No model family or post-hoc tuning search was added.

## 6.1 LDA and QDA

```{r fit-discriminant-models}
set.seed(SEED)
fit_lda <- train(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ ., data = model_data, method = "lda",
  metric = "ROC", maximize = TRUE, trControl = ctrl,
  preProcess = c("center", "scale")
)

set.seed(SEED)
fit_qda <- train(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ ., data = model_data, method = "qda",
  metric = "ROC", maximize = TRUE, trControl = ctrl,
  preProcess = c("center", "scale")
)
```

## 6.2 Linear and RBF SVM

```{r fit-svm-models}
grid_svm_linear <- expand.grid(C = 2^seq(-5, 5, by = 1))

set.seed(SEED)
fit_svm_linear <- train(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ ., data = model_data, method = "svmLinear",
  metric = "ROC", maximize = TRUE, trControl = ctrl,
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"), tuneGrid = grid_svm_linear
)

set.seed(SEED)
fit_svm_rbf <- train(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ ., data = model_data, method = "svmRadial",
  metric = "ROC", maximize = TRUE, trControl = ctrl,
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"), tuneLength = 10
)
```

## 6.3 ANN

The coursework used neuralnet. The update uses nnet so the ANN follows the same
caret resampling and fold-internal preprocessing. This is a standardized ANN
comparison, not an exact reproduction of the original network implementation.

```{r fit-ann}
grid_ann <- expand.grid(
  size = c(1, 3, 5),
  decay = c(0, 0.001, 0.01, 0.1)
)

set.seed(SEED)
fit_ann <- train(
  DEATH_EVENT ~ ., data = model_data, method = "nnet",
  metric = "ROC", maximize = TRUE, trControl = ctrl,
  preProcess = c("center", "scale"), tuneGrid = grid_ann,
  trace = FALSE, maxit = 1000, MaxNWts = 10000
)
```

```{r selected-tuning}
selected_tuning <- bind_rows(
  LDA = fit_lda$bestTune,
  QDA = fit_qda$bestTune,
  "Linear SVM" = fit_svm_linear$bestTune,
  "RBF SVM" = fit_svm_rbf$bestTune,
  ANN = fit_ann$bestTune,
  .id = "Model"
)

knitr::kable(selected_tuning, digits = 7)
```

# 7. Repeated cross-validation results

```{r performance-table}
metrics <- c(
  "ROC", "Sensitivity", "Specificity", "Balanced_Accuracy", "Accuracy"
)

summarise_fit <- function(fit, model_name) {
  fit$resample |>
    summarise(across(all_of(metrics), ~ mean(.x, na.rm = TRUE))) |>
    mutate(Model = model_name, .before = 1)
}

performance_table <- bind_rows(
  summarise_fit(fit_lda, "LDA"),
  summarise_fit(fit_qda, "QDA"),
  summarise_fit(fit_svm_linear, "Linear SVM"),
  summarise_fit(fit_svm_rbf, "RBF SVM"),
  summarise_fit(fit_ann, "ANN")
) |>
  rename(
    "ROC-AUC" = ROC,
    "Balanced Accuracy" = Balanced_Accuracy
  )

knitr::kable(performance_table, digits = 3)
```

```{r model-auc-resamples, fig.cap="ROC-AUC distributions across the 25 validation resamples."}
auc_resamples <- bind_rows(
  fit_lda$resample |> transmute(Model = "LDA", Resample, ROC),
  fit_qda$resample |> transmute(Model = "QDA", Resample, ROC),
  fit_svm_linear$resample |> transmute(Model = "Linear SVM", Resample, ROC),
  fit_svm_rbf$resample |> transmute(Model = "RBF SVM", Resample, ROC),
  fit_ann$resample |> transmute(Model = "ANN", Resample, ROC)
) |>
  mutate(
    Model = factor(
      Model,
      levels = c("LDA", "QDA", "Linear SVM", "RBF SVM", "ANN")
    )
  )

auc_plot <- ggplot(auc_resamples, aes(Model, ROC, fill = Model)) +
  geom_boxplot(width = 0.65, outlier.shape = NA, alpha = 0.85) +
  geom_jitter(width = 0.12, alpha = 0.45, size = 1.4) +
  scale_fill_brewer(palette = "Set2", guide = "none") +
  labs(x = NULL, y = "ROC-AUC") +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(
  file.path(FIGURE_PATH, "model_auc_resamples.png"),
  auc_plot,
  width = 8,
  height = 5,
  dpi = 180
)

auc_plot
```

RBF SVM has the highest mean ROC-AUC. ANN has the highest sensitivity and
balanced accuracy. LDA and linear SVM have high specificity but low sensitivity
for deaths. Model preference depends on the evaluation objective and the relative
cost of false negatives and false positives. Accuracy or training error alone is
not sufficient for selection.

# 8. Exploratory threshold analysis

```{r oof-roc}
rbf_pred <- fit_svm_rbf$pred |>
  filter(
    C == fit_svm_rbf$bestTune$C,
    sigma == fit_svm_rbf$bestTune$sigma
  )

ann_pred <- fit_ann$pred |>
  filter(
    size == fit_ann$bestTune$size,
    decay == fit_ann$bestTune$decay
  )

roc_rbf <- roc(
  response = rbf_pred$obs,
  predictor = rbf_pred$Died,
  levels = c("Survived", "Died"),
  direction = "<"
)

roc_ann <- roc(
  response = ann_pred$obs,
  predictor = ann_pred$Died,
  levels = c("Survived", "Died"),
  direction = "<"
)

roc_plot <- pROC::ggroc(
  list("RBF SVM" = roc_rbf, ANN = roc_ann),
  legacy.axes = TRUE,
  linewidth = 1
) +
  geom_abline(intercept = 0, slope = 1, linetype = 3, color = "grey60") +
  scale_color_manual(values = c("RBF SVM" = "#C44E52", ANN = "#4C72B0")) +
  coord_equal() +
  labs(
    x = "1 - Specificity",
    y = "Sensitivity",
    color = "Model",
    title = "Exploratory pooled out-of-fold ROC curves"
  ) +
  theme_minimal(base_size = 11) +
  theme(legend.position = "bottom", panel.grid.minor = element_blank())

ggsave(
  file.path(FIGURE_PATH, "roc_rbf_vs_ann.png"),
  roc_plot,
  width = 7,
  height = 6,
  dpi = 180
)

roc_plot
```

```{r thresholds}
coords_rbf <- coords(
  roc_rbf, x = "best", best.method = "youden",
  ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity")
)

coords_ann <- coords(
  roc_ann, x = "best", best.method = "youden",
  ret = c("threshold", "sensitivity", "specificity")
)

threshold_comparison <- tibble(
  Model = c("RBF SVM", "ANN"),
  Pooled_OOF_AUC = c(as.numeric(auc(roc_rbf)), as.numeric(auc(roc_ann))),
  Threshold = c(
    as.numeric(coords_rbf$threshold),
    as.numeric(coords_ann$threshold)
  ),
  Sensitivity = c(
    as.numeric(coords_rbf$sensitivity),
    as.numeric(coords_ann$sensitivity)
  ),
  Specificity = c(
    as.numeric(coords_rbf$specificity),
    as.numeric(coords_ann$specificity)
  )
)

knitr::kable(threshold_comparison, digits = 3)
```

Each patient appears once per repeat in the pooled out-of-fold predictions.
Therefore, these pooled ROC curves and Youden thresholds are exploratory
summaries of repeated predictions, not independent validation results and not
clinical thresholds. The primary comparison remains the mean of 25
resample-level metrics.

# 9. What changed

| Item | Original coursework | Validation update |
|---|---|---|
| SVM evaluation | Training-set prediction | Repeated cross-validation |
| Model comparison | Different validation schemes | Identical resampling folds |
| Preprocessing | ANN scaled before splitting | Estimated inside training folds |
| QDA priors | Reversed relative to factor order | Empirical priors in common workflow |
| Metrics | Mainly misclassification rate | AUC, sensitivity, specificity, balanced accuracy, accuracy |
| Conclusion | RBF SVM appeared dominant | Model choice depends on the objective |

# 10. Interpretation

The original 2.68% RBF SVM error does not estimate performance on unseen data.
Under a common repeated cross-validation design, the performance gap is smaller
and the models show different error profiles. RBF SVM provides the strongest
average rank discrimination in this run. ANN identifies a larger share of deaths
and has the highest balanced accuracy. LDA and linear SVM favor correct
classification of survivors at the cost of lower death sensitivity.

This is classification of DEATH_EVENT, not formal survival analysis,
independent risk-factor inference, or evidence of clinical utility.

# 11. Limitations

- The sample contains 299 patients and 96 deaths.
- The dataset is observational.
- No external validation dataset is used.
- Hyperparameter selection and performance estimation are not separated by
  nested cross-validation, so modest optimistic bias may remain.
- The pooled repeated-CV threshold analysis is exploratory.
- The analysis classifies DEATH_EVENT. It is not survival analysis and does not
  estimate mortality at a fixed time horizon.
- Six continuous variables were retained for the coursework comparison.
- The ANN implementation changed from neuralnet to nnet to support common
  resampling.
